samples.question: This image shows five square panels of the same size standing side by side in one row, each framed in grey and numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel holds exactly the same three things: an orange dot, a straight green beam that starts at that orange dot and stops where it meets a straight blue bar, and one red disk. The blue bar is a mirror. Within a scene the blue bars all have the same length, the green beams all have the same length and the red disks all have the same size, so length, size, colour, count and the amount of ink carry no information. The green beam does not pass through the mirror: at the point where it meets the blue bar it reflects, leaving on the other side of the point at the same angle to the bar as it arrived, and then travels on in a perfectly straight line. That reflected part of the path is never drawn, so it has to be worked out. Exactly one panel is arranged so that its reflected beam runs into that panel's red disk; in each of the other four panels the reflected beam passes the red disk and misses it by at least 10 pixels of clearance. The undrawn straight continuation of the beam through the mirror, without reflecting, misses the red disk in every panel, so ignoring the mirror never gives the answer. In every panel the beam meets the blue bar well inside the bar's two ends, and the red disk touches neither the beam nor the bar. Where the mirror sits, how it is tilted, which side the beam comes from and where the red disk lies are all free to vary from panel to panel. Which numbered panel is the one whose reflected beam runs into its red disk? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.
